- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then overcorrects, leading to overshoot followed by sharp downward revision.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually adjusts downward.
- When true values show strong mean reversion (e.g., after a spike), model fails to recognize the pullback and continues to project upward.
- Model underreacts to sharp downward moves in the history, often missing the magnitude of the drop in the forecast.
- Forecast tends to lag behind true values by 2–5 days, especially in the middle of the horizon.
- Model overestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days, leading to overcorrection and underprediction of true values.
- When history shows a clear downward trend, model often fails to recognize the trend’s continuation and overestimates recovery.
- Model is prone to “overfitting” recent spikes, projecting them into future values even when context suggests a correction is imminent.
